text:
alice: Quick heads-up 1: I'm opening a docs PR to tighten up the Function/Tool Calling examples. The full verbose JSON examples are great for reference but they're noisy for SDK quickstarts. Will propose compact envelopes + a link to a verbose appendix.
ben: Sounds good. Are you planning to change field names in examples? we should keep compatibility notes if we rename anything.
tanya: +1 to compact. A small appendix with the full schema (100% identical to runtime output) would be ideal for integrators.
alice: Plan: replace most inline examples in the guide with 3-line compact envelopes, add one full example in /docs/appendix/structured-output-full.md, and update python/js snippets to match. Also add a 1-line fallback snippet showing how to handle raw_text when parsing fails.
ben: For the fallback, show pattern: try parse envelope -> if missing, fallback to raw_text -> do best-effort parse. Keeps code clear.
ryan: ops note: the runtime currently emits `invocation` for new models; older SDKs used `tool_call`. Docs should show `invocation` as canonical but mention `tool_call` in a parenthetical.
infra-bot: Reminder: add a CHANGELOG entry and mark PR docs-only to skip build gating.
tanya: Also found a broken anchor in the JSON Schema section when I clicked from the migration guide. Please include that link fix in the same PR.
alice: I'll patch the anchor and update the migration guide cross-link to the compact example + appendix. I'll also update snippets/python/invoke_quickstart.md and snippets/js/compact_invoke.md.
ben: Nice. Can we add a tiny lint in docs CI to ensure every invoke snippet contains either `compact` or `raw_text` so we don't regress? A grep + exit non-zero if not found.
ryan: good idea. Ops will review the CI check. Also request: avoid changing public API examples without a clear compatibility note at the top of the page.
tanya: For the compact envelope example, propose this minimal shape in docs:
```json
{"invocation": {"id": "123", "tool": "weather"}, "output": {"compact": {"temp": 68, "unit": "F"}, "raw_text": "Temp is 68F"}}
```
ben: That's clear. For SDKs show parsing pattern (py):
```python
resp = client.invoke(...)
out = resp['output'].get('compact')
if not out:
    # fallback
    out = parse_text(resp['output'].get('raw_text', ''))
```
tanya: Short sentence under the snippet: "Use the compact field for deterministic parsing; raw_text is a fallback for models that returned unstructured text."
alice: I'll also do a grep for `tool_call` across /snippets and /docs and open small PRs to update legacy occurrences to the compat note.
infra-bot: CI run queued: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/actions/runs/1122334455
ben: I'll review the PR when ready. If it's small and tests pass, feel free to merge after one approval.
tanya: I'll scan for any other broken links after you push.
alice: Pushing P.R. now. Title: "docs: compact invoke examples + appendix + migration links" (no emojis).
ryan: thanks. Quick reminder to include a short changelog blurb: "docs: clarify compact envelope usage and add appendix".
alice: done, changelog entry added. PR updated with link fixes, snippet updates, CI lint. Requesting reviews from @ben and @tanya.
ben: Reviewing now.
tanya: LGTM pending the grep pass.
infra-bot: PR updated: link fixes, snippets modified, changelog added. Merge queued after approvals.
